#Review of the test system

Date: 2026-11-12. Method: static review. Nothing was built or run.

Sources: src/tools/test_all, src/e2e, src/tools/e2e, src/tools/wpt, src/tools/test262, the unit tests, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and three CI logs of 2026-11-09 kept in build/ (ci_win.log, ci_win2.log, ci_win3.log, ci_linux.log).

Each finding gives a location, the cost, and a fix. Findings are ordered by gain in each section. A time marked "measured" comes from the CI logs. A time marked "estimate" is a calculation from those numbers.

#Summary

The tests are mostly built on conditions. The lint of sleeps works. Fixed delays are not the main cost.

The main costs are these:

  1. The Windows runner is saturated. test_all takes 1810 s with 100 % of its two slots busy and 3.8 of 4 processors in use (measured). A shorter wait does not help there. Less CPU work or more runners help.
  2. One job runs everything. Three groups of steps do not depend on each other and can run on three runners.
  3. Bounds are long. A failed barrier costs 240 s. A stuck step costs 900 s. Some steps have a bound of 4 hours. Some waits have no bound.
  4. Nothing stops a run in which the same failure repeats in every step. This is the most probable cause of a job that reaches its 90 minutes.

Expected gains:

ChangeWindows jobLinux jobLocal run
Split the Windows job in three (3.1)34 min to 14-16 min (estimate)
No software frames for tests that read no pixel (4.1)minus 3 to 4 min before the split (estimate)minus some CPU
Cache the JavaScript engine on Linux (4.3)minus 3 min (measured)
Cache the test server programs (4.4)minus 1 min (estimate)
One sweep of the check build, not two (4.2)minus 5 min or more (estimate)
Short deadlines and a circuit breaker (2.1, 2.2)worst case 90 min to 45 min; a failing test 240 s to 60 ssamesame
e2e_test does not wait for the browser build (3.2)minus 18 to 107 s after a change of the browser

#Measured baseline

Windows job, run ci_win3.log (4 vCPU, -Jobs 2):

  • Setup and caches: 150 s. wrentool build: 64 s. test_all: 1810 s. Total: about 34 min.
  • test_all: 3871 s of steps, 6787 s of CPU, 1707 processes, 211 steps.

The steps that use the most CPU (measured):

StepWallCPU
Local pages on the check build (wrentool sweep)376 s964 s
Check build: scripted session and endurance278 s760 s
busy_page (two steps)222 s428 s
cursor185 s265 s
Build of e2e_test81 s240 s
text_decoration74 s233 s
inline_svg_hover (failed on a capture timeout)139 s202 s
web-platform-tests220 s172 s
Build of the test server, and go test135 s + 122 s68 s + 75 s
Unit tests on poisoned memory: style131 s103 s

Linux job, run ci_linux.log: test_all takes 117 s. The step "Native libraries" takes 216 s. In that step, buildjs takes 177 s. The job has no cache for the engine.

#1. Fixed delays and waits that are not conditions

The lint src/tools/test_all/lint_sleeps.odin finds time.sleep. It does not find the forms below. The total cost per run is 15 to 25 s of real time, spread over parallel steps. The gain in wall clock is small. The gain in reliability is larger: each item below depends on the speed of the machine.

#1.1 wait_at_rest costs 500 ms at each call

  • Location: src/e2e/e2e.odin:58 (REST_QUIET), src/e2e/e2e.odin:519.
  • Callers: devtools_fold.odin:66, menu_wheel.odin:36, pointer_gesture.odin:113, scroll_driven.odin:299, and six calls in frames_at_rest.odin.
  • Cost: 0.5 s of real time at each call, in each run. The wait ends only when the time has passed.
  • Fix: ask the browser for the state. Add a field at_rest to api.Stats: no frame is requested, no animation runs, no timer that draws is armed. Wait for that field with wait_until. Keep REST_QUIET only in frames_at_rest.odin, where the absence of frames in real time is the subject.

#1.2 busy_wait is a fixed delay in real time

  • Location: src/e2e/busy.odin:44. Callers: busy_page.odin:278 (300 ms), busy_page.odin:344 (400 ms), busy_page.odin:408 (5 waits of 90 ms), chrome_frames.odin:323 (100 ms).
  • Cost: about 1.3 s per run. The larger cost is the flaky test of 5.2.
  • Fix: use busy_clock(ms) for each of them. scroll_driven.odin does this for animations. The caret and the autoscroll must read the clock of the chrome frame for that.

#1.3 Sections cut short at a set time

  • Location: src/tools/e2e/web_jsweb.odin:325. 37 sections, each abandoned after 0, 10, 100 and 300 ms.
  • Cost: about 15 s of real waits per run (37 x 0.41 s), in three steps.
  • Fix: cut on an event count, not on a time. Close the page after N turns of the loop (0, 1, 10, 100). The result does not depend on the machine then, and the steps take milliseconds.

#1.4 A hung GPU process is waited for 10 s

  • Location: src/tools/e2e/webgl_process.odin:19 (HANG_MS :: 10_000), used at lines 123, 152, 175, 277.
  • Cost: 10 s of real time in the test of the hung process. The comment says 1 s and 3 s failed under load.
  • Fix: give the watcher an injectable clock. The test advances that clock past the limit after the process hangs.

#1.5 A second start waits 3 s for a first one that does not answer

  • Location: src/tools/e2e/instance.odin:136. The test passes only when the product's 3 s timeout expires.
  • Cost: 2.5 to 9 s per run.
  • Fix: make the hand-over timeout a preference of the launch (browser.instance.answer_ms), set to 100 ms in this test. The test still proves the path. This is not a variable only for tests: it is the product's limit.

#1.6 WebSocket closing handshake: 50 repetitions

  • Location: src/tools/e2e/web_wsclose.odin:17 (RUNS :: 50), line 165 (3 runs x 300 ms), line 154 (5 runs x 200 ms server delay).
  • Cost: 39 s on the CI (measured). The file says the repetitions make a race of one in two "certain to show".
  • Fix: 10 runs give a detection probability of 99.9 % for a race of one in two. Use RUNS :: 10. Replace closedelay=200 with a gate of the test server (?gate=K). Gain: about 30 s of a light slot.

#1.7 Real server delays in the web tests

  • Locations: web_jsload.odin:35-43 (delays of 5 to 300 ms, one of 3000 ms), web_jsload.odin:53 (COMPILE_TAKES_IT_MS :: 500), web_sitecompat.odin:26-27, web_net.odin:61 (BURST_SERVER_MS :: 400), web_net.odin:52 (500 ms receive timeout, run for each of two backends), download.odin:17.
  • Cost: 2 to 4 s per run. Each "A arrives before B" proven by two delays fails on a slow runner.
  • Fix: use gates. The test opens gate A, waits for the event, then opens gate B. The order is then a fact. The receive timeout in web_net.odin:268 is a real client timer: it can stay.

#1.8 Other real waits

  • src/tools/e2e/remote_channel.odin:81: 1 s sleep to measure CPU of a Wren with no channel. This is a measure of time. Move it behind base.perf_skip, as the two other sleeps of the file.
  • src/tools/e2e/remote_channel.odin:96: 300 ms sleep. Replace it with a condition on the channel's state.
  • src/tools/e2e/urlbar.odin:127: a 400 ms busy loop in the page. Hold the page until a condition, as chrome_frames.odin does with hold().
  • src/tools/e2e/crash_recovery.odin:16-18: snapshot timers of 500 ms and 1000 ms in real time. Lower both preferences to 20 ms, or give the session writer the loop's virtual clock.
  • src/tools/e2e/frames_at_rest.odin:20: REST_TURNS :: 120 turns of at least 1 ms. Legitimate: the subject is what the browser does in real time. The step is .No_CI.

#1.9 base.await spins on a processor

  • Location: src/base/await.odin:17-24. 15 callers in unit tests.
  • Cost: the wait calls thread.yield() in a loop. It uses a full processor during the wait. With 12 jobs, each spinning test slows the other steps. The limit is 60 s.
  • Fix: wait on a sync.Futex or a semaphore with a timeout of 1 ms between looks. The condition stays the same. Add base.await( and thread.yield( loops to the patterns of lint_sleeps.odin.

#1.10 The lint does not see every wait

  • Location: src/tools/test_all/lint_sleeps.odin:15 (TEST_SLEEP_CALLS).
  • Missing patterns: thread.yield( (images_test.odin:335, webaudio/worklet_test.odin:38), busy_wait(, wait_at_rest(, rest_turns(, sema_wait_with_timeout(, futex_wait_with_timeout(, and a loop on tick_since(...) < with loop_wait (web_workers.odin:457, web_jsweb.odin:325).
  • Fix: add these patterns. Each remaining use then has a line and a reason in tools/test_sleeps_allowed.txt.

#Legitimate bounded waits (no change)

  • e2e.wait_for (src/e2e/process.odin:190): 5 ms poll on what another process does. It ends on the condition.
  • web_harness.wait_until (web_harness.odin:124): loop_wait of 5 ms that any event ends sooner.
  • wait_frames(s, 2): 174 uses. Frames are made at once. No use asks for more than a few frames.
  • The scheduler's 10 ms tick and the WPT parent's 50 ms tick.

#2. Bounds that are too long, and hangs that are not detected

#2.1 No circuit breaker: one cause can cost 100 steps x 240 s

  • Locations: src/e2e/e2e.odin:44-46 (TEST_LIMIT 5 min, DEFAULT_DEADLINE 4 min), src/tools/e2e/web_harness.odin:39-40 (the same), src/tools/test_all/main.odin:26 (900 s per step).
  • Scenario: the software rasterizer, the test server library or the engine image fails on the runner. Each of the 77 end-to-end steps and 22 web steps then waits 240 to 300 s, two at a time. That is more than 3 hours of work. The job stops at 90 minutes with no report.
  • This is the most probable cause of the 90-minute runs. The design test: break testserver.dll and run the CI.
  • Fix, in scheduler.odin: count the steps that end as stuck or with "Test timed out". After 5 of them, stop admitting steps that have the same needs. Mark the others NOT RUN: 5 steps timed out. Write the report.
  • Fix, in ci.yml:70: add timeout-minutes: 45 to the step "Tests". Add a flag -RunTimeoutSec 2400 to test_all: past it, the scheduler dumps and kills every running step, then writes its report.
  • Fix, in ci.yml: upload build/test_logs, build/test_report.txt and build/e2e/*/failure.png with if: always(). A cancelled job leaves nothing to read today.

#2.2 A failed barrier costs 240 s, and a web test continues after it

  • Location: src/tools/e2e/web_harness.odin:124-134. wait_until records a failure and returns false. Most callers ignore the result. A test with three waits costs 720 s, cut at 300 s by TEST_LIMIT.
  • Then the runner ends the thread. The world of the process (loop, pages, storage) is left in the middle of a call. Each later test of the process waits on that broken world. The step ends at its 900 s limit.
  • Measured example: inline_svg_hover failed in 139 s on a capture timeout (ci_win.log, ci_win3.log).
  • Fix: one deadline of 60 s in both harnesses, and a test limit of 90 s. The CI's slowest passing step takes 186 s for 40 elements: no single barrier is near 60 s. Measure the longest barrier of a CI run first: WREN_E2E_TRACE=1 prints each call with its time.
  • Fix: make the first timeout of a web test final. wait_until sets a package flag broken, as src/e2e/e2e.odin:135 does. begin fails at once when the flag is set. The step then ends in seconds.
  • Fix: process.odin:63 (PROCESS_WAIT_MS = 4 min) is used in cleanups (process.odin:79, process.odin:143). A cleanup must not wait 4 minutes for a process that it has killed. Use 10 s there.

#2.3 Tasks cannot be killed: a hung build has no bound

  • Location: src/tools/test_all/scheduler.odin:468-481. For a stuck task, the scheduler sets task.kill. Only task_exec (scheduler.odin:443) reads that flag.
  • These tasks do not use task_exec: task_browser, task_dependencies, task_js_engine, task_launcher, task_testserver, task_runner (tasks.odin:13-76). They call tooling.run with no limit (src/tools/wrentool/builder/builder.odin:209).
  • Result: a compiler that does not end keeps the run alive for ever. ci.yml:41-42 describes this exact event for the dev build and gives that step 20 minutes. The check build inside test_all (steps.odin:248) has the same compiler and no bound.
  • Fix: one way to start a process from a task. tooling.run takes a ^bool kill flag and a limit. builder.Options carries both. The scheduler's limit then ends every child. Remove the second path.
  • Fix: after a task is told to stop, give it 60 s. Then mark the step stuck, finish it, and let the thread go. The run must end even if a thread does not.

#2.4 Step limits of 4 hours on the CI

  • Location: src/tools/test_all/steps.odin:106 (LONG_STEP_SECONDS :: 4 * 3600). Used at lines 241, 247, 248, 375, 377, 397, 449, 483, 498, 503 and in asan.odin:154.
  • The CI jobs have limits of 45 to 90 minutes. A limit of 4 hours is no limit there.
  • Fix: a limit per step from its measured time. Under -Quick or -CI: 10 minutes for a build, 15 minutes for WPT, test262 and the endurance run. Keep 4 hours only for full runs. Step.limit becomes a procedure of cfg.

#2.5 The first WPT child is waited for without a bound

  • Location: src/tools/wpt/queue.odin:257. os.process_wait has no timeout. This child compiles the engine image and writes the disk cache.
  • Second case: queue.odin:269. A child is declared hung only when len(c.handed) > 0. A child in the Draining phase that has reported every test and does not exit keeps busy true for ever.
  • Fix: poll the first child with the same hang limit as the others. Remove the condition on handed: a child with nothing in hand and no exit after hang_ms is killed. Its exit is not a CRASH of a test.

#2.6 test262 waits for its threads without a bound

  • Location: src/tools/test262/main.odin:763-770. The loop waits for every worker thread. A test is stopped by the engine's interrupt flag, which is cooperative. A native call that does not return is never stopped.
  • Fix: each worker publishes the start time of its current test. The main loop fails the run when one test has run for more than 10 times -timeout. It prints the test's name and exits with a code other than 0.

#2.7 A unit test has no time limit

  • Fact: no *_test.odin file under src calls testing.set_fail_timeout (0 of 296 files). core:testing gives a test no limit by default.
  • Result: a unit test that hangs costs the step limit, 900 s, and the log does not name the test.
  • Fix: build every unit step with -define:ODIN_TEST_LOG_STATE_CHANGES=true (as the ASan steps do), so that the log names the test that was running. Set the step limit of a unit step to 10 times its last duration, with a floor of 120 s. build/test_all_times.txt has the durations.

#2.8 A second failure in one e2e process waits for ever

  • Location: src/e2e/e2e.odin:307-311 and docs/testing.md ("the next signal waits for ever"). stop_test avoids the defect of core:testing on Windows. An assertion or a fault in a test does not.
  • Result: after two faults in one process, the process hangs until the step limit (900 s).
  • Fix: do not depend on the runner here. In e2e, install the assertion handler of the session (s.ctx.assertion_failure_proc) to log the message and call stop_test. For a fault, the crash handler of wb:tools/crashtrace ends the process at once: with one process per file, the rest of the file is NOT RUN and is said so. This is a bounded and visible result.

#2.9 Smaller unbounded waits

  • src/tools/test_all/tasks.odin:252: tooling.wait(&p) on build/fetch with no limit, in a task that cannot be killed. Fix: tooling.wait(&p, 120 * time.Second).
  • src/tools/tooling/process.odin:106: capture has no limit. It runs git, node, vswhere, and in asan.odin:69 a whole compile of the browser while it holds a mutex that three steps wait on. Fix: a limit parameter with a default of 60 s; 20 minutes for the call of asan.odin:69.
  • src/tools/test_all/scheduler.odin:533-537: after kill_tree, the scheduler waits for poll with no bound. Fix: after 30 s, release the process and finish the step.
  • src/tools/wpt/queue.odin:249 and :272: process_wait after a kill, with no timeout. Fix: 30 s.

#3. Parallelism

#3.1 Split the Windows job in three

  • Location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:17-76.
  • Fact: the job is bound by CPU, not by waits. -Jobs 3 and -Jobs 4 were measured slower (ci.yml:52-56). More runners are the only way to more parallelism.

  • Three groups with no dependency between them (measured CPU of ci_win3.log):

    • A, the check build: wrentool build check, the sweep, the scripted session, the endurance run, remote_check. About 1800 s of CPU, 27 % of the run.
    • B, the browser shell: the 77 e2e_step steps. About 2700 s of CPU.
    • C, everything else: unit tests, web tests, WPT, toolkit suites, lints, the package. About 2300 s of CPU.
  • Each job pays the setup (150 s), and B also pays wrentool build (64 s) and the build of e2e_test (81 s).
  • Result (estimate): the longest job takes 14 to 16 minutes, against 34 minutes.
  • Fix: use -Only and -Except with three patterns, as the asan and test262 jobs do. Give Step a field group so that the patterns do not depend on step names. test_all -List must print the group.
  • Option: one build job uploads build/wren.exe, build/e2e_test.exe, build/testserver.* and build/native as an artifact. The three jobs download it. This removes 150 to 300 s of CPU per job.

#3.2 The build of e2e_test waits for the browser build

  • Location: src/tools/test_all/steps.odin:422 (needs = COMMON_NEEDS + {.Browser}), and line 483 for WPT.
  • The comment says the program links build/native, "which the browser's build makes". The step of line 241 makes .Native, and COMMON_NEEDS contains .Native.
  • Cost: locally, after a change of a browser source, e2e_test starts only when wren.exe is linked. That is 18 to 107 s of critical path (the times of the dev build in AGENTS.md). No cost on the CI: the browser is built before.
  • Fix: verify that builder.dependencies leaves build/native in its final state. Then remove .Browser from the two needs. If the browser build changes build/native after that, move that work to builder.dependencies: two steps must not write one product.

#3.3 The network test runs its two backends one after the other

  • Location: src/tools/test_all/steps.odin:463-464. Two web_run("net", ...) actions in one step.
  • Cost: about 25 s in one light slot. The two runs share nothing: each has its own process and port block.
  • Fix: two steps, one per backend. Gain: about 12 s when a light slot is free.

#3.4 ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1

  • E2E_BUILD_FLAGS (steps.odin:102-104): needed. The browser's state is the process's. The split by file, and each_test for five files, give the parallelism. No change.
  • steps.odin:254 (images): one test sets the idle time of the process-wide decoder pool. Fix: the pool takes its settings at creation, and the test makes its own pool. The step takes 3 s: low gain, but it removes a shared global.
  • steps.odin:271-274 (remote, remote api, remote client), steps.odin:363 (wasm), steps.odin:414-419 (toolkit suites): each step takes 1 to 8 s. No gain worth a change.

#3.5 Shared resources

  • Ports: solved. A block of ports per process, from the worktree's path (docs/testing.md, "The test server").
  • Profiles: solved. e2e.temp_profile, and build/web_profile/<pid> (web_harness.odin:38).
  • build/wrentool_step.exe: three steps build the same file (steps.odin:236, :452, :492). In a full local run, the steps of lines 236 and 452 run at the same time and write the same file. See 4.5.
  • build/tmp/license_tool_test.wrenlicense (tasks.odin:134): a fixed name. Two runs in one worktree collide. Fix: add the pid to the name, as tasks.odin:210 does.
  • The GPU: on the CI every frame is drawn by the software rasterizer. See 4.1.

#3.6 Order of a run

  • The scheduler starts the longest path first (scheduler.odin:279-287). This is correct.
  • On the CI, the test server took 136 s to build, and the 99 steps that need it waited (measured). The two heavy slots stayed busy with unit tests, so no slot was idle. See 4.4 for the fix.
  • The first run on a runner has no durations (build/test_all_times.txt is not cached). Each step is then taken for its weight or 60 s. Fix: commit a file of typical CI durations, or cache the file between runs.

#4. Redundant or wasteful work

#4.1 The software rasterizer draws frames that no test reads

  • Fact: on a runner a frame takes 15 to 22 ms to draw, against 0.1 ms on a GPU (docs/testing.md).
  • Example: src/tools/e2e/cursor.odin:33-45. For each of 40 elements the test asks for frames, then reads stats.cursor. It reads no pixel. It takes 185 s and 265 s of CPU on the CI (measured), at a scale of 2.
  • The chrome world already has this idea: "no renderer unless the test asks for pixels" (chrome_world.odin:108), 7 to 40 ms a test.
  • Fix: e2e.Options.pixels. Without it, the session builds the display list and skips the rasterization. e2e.capture fails with a clear message in such a session. Start with cursor, config, page_scrollbars (if it reads geometry), keyboard_owner, search, urlbar, history.
  • Gain (estimate): 600 to 900 s of CPU on the CI, 3 to 4 minutes of the unsplit job.

#4.2 The sweep of the check build runs on both systems, and costs the most

  • Locations: steps.odin:451-452 (Windows: 376 s, 964 s of CPU, measured), ci.yml:259-263 (Linux: a full ./build.sh check, then the sweep under xvfb and a software Vulkan driver).
  • Every end-to-end test already runs with freed memory poisoned (steps.odin:422, POISON).
  • Fix: run the sweep in one place per system, in a job of its own (group A of 3.1 on Windows, a second Linux job). The main jobs then do not wait for it.
  • Fix: the sweep passes -CloseMs 60000 -PingMs 60000. Check that no page waits for one of these limits in a passing run: 14 pages in 376 s is 27 s per page.

#4.3 The Linux job builds the JavaScript engine in every run

  • Location: ci.yml:239-248. buildjs took 177 s (measured, ci_linux.log 00:02:36 to 00:05:33).
  • The Windows setup caches build/js (.github/actions/setup/action.yml, "Cache the JavaScript engine").
  • Fix: the same actions/cache step in the Linux job, with the same key and a linux- prefix. Cache build/wasmtime-linux, build/lexbor-linux and the wgpu archive too. Gain: about 3 minutes.
  • Fix: the apt-get and LLVM steps run in every job. Build a container image with them once (ghcr.io/.../wren-ci:bookworm-llvm18) and use it in container:. Gain: 1 to 2 minutes (estimate).

#4.4 The test server is compiled three times with no Go cache

  • Location: .github/actions/setup/action.yml:48-51 (cache: false), steps.odin:442-443.
  • Cost: "build testserver" 135 s and go test 122 s (measured). The DLL, the program and the test binary compile the same packages (quic-go, HTTP/2) from nothing.
  • Fix: cache build/testserver.exe and build/testserver.dll with a key from tools/testserver/**. A hit makes the step a no-op, as for Lexbor. Also set cache: true with cache-dependency-path: tools/testserver/go.sum for the build cache.
  • Gain: 140 s of CPU, and the end-to-end steps can start 2 minutes sooner.

#4.5 wrentool is built up to five times

  • Locations: ci.yml:35, ci.yml:106, ci.yml:143, and steps.odin:236, :452, :492 (build/wrentool_step.exe).
  • Fix: one step that makes a product .Wrentool (build/wrentool_step.exe). The three steps need it. This also removes the two writers of 3.5. In ci.yml:106, remove the second build: the file of line 35 is still there.
  • The same for src/tools/license: steps.odin:433 and :435 build it twice under two names. One product.

#4.6 Packages compiled and tested two to four times

  • base, style, layout: a normal step (steps.odin:250-256), a poisoned step (:257-259) and an ASan step (asan.odin:20). page: normal, poisoned with pages (:281-284) and ASan.
  • Measured on the CI: style 31 s and 131 s; layout 50 s and 54 s.
  • The two variants run the same tests. The poisoned build detects more. The normal build is what ships.
  • Fix (option): on the CI, run only the poisoned variant of these three packages. Keep both in a full run. Gain: about 80 s of step time. Decide this with care: the allocators differ between the two builds.

#4.7 odin check of each package on Linux

  • Location: src/tools/test_all/steps_linux.odin:18-19 and :39-43. 46 checks.
  • odin check src/tools/e2e type-checks every package that it imports. Most of the 46 checks repeat that work.
  • Cost: small (0 to 2 s each, about 30 s of CPU). Fix: keep the leaf programs (tools/e2e, tools/wpt, tools/endurance, tools/test_all, tools/crashtrace) and the packages that no program imports. Verify first that -vet applies to imported packages of the wb collection.

#4.8 Tests that are benchmarks

  • The four bench_*_test.odin files (src/browser, src/layout) are opt-in by a define or a variable. Good.
  • The measures in the end-to-end files are behind base.perf_skip (12 places). Good.
  • src/tools/test_all/steps.odin:378-397: the JIT step runs 15 jsengine commands on examples/jsbench files, then the whole of test262 with the JIT. It is in its own CI job. No change.
  • src/tools/e2e/busy_page.odin: 428 s of CPU on the CI (measured), because pages hold a thread in a busy loop for a real duration. With busy_clock (1.2) the holds can be short. Gain (estimate): 200 s of CPU.

#5. Tests that depend on something they must not depend on

#5.1 State built by hand in three ways

  • app_start (src/browser/main.odin:1687) is the product's constructor.
  • test_app (src/browser/app_test.odin:10) is a second one. 279 uses.
  • chrome_start (src/tools/e2e/chrome_world.odin:77-125) is a third. It repeats the list of *_init calls of the product and builds each Tab by hand (:115-120), with the comment "as tab_new does".
  • 18 unit tests call new(App) directly, and others call new(Tab) or new(Browser_Window): about_wren_test.odin:278, bench_palette_test.odin:26, chrome_style_test.odin:251, demos_test.odin:47, desktop_shell_test.odin:39 and :66, devtools_test.odin:30 and :128, download_test.odin:13, history_tree_test.odin:176, local_paths_test_windows.odin:43, pacing_test.odin:129, palette_test.odin:98, selection_shell_test.odin:8, urlbar_test.odin:219 and :321, wheel_step_test_windows.odin:9, windows_test.odin:86 (with tab_ids filled by hand at :168).
  • This is the cause of the two harnesses that broke on tab_ids.
  • Fix: one constructor in stages, in src/browser. app_make(Options) makes an App that satisfies every invariant with no window. app_chrome_init(app, window) adds what the interface reads. app_start calls both, then the rest. test_app and chrome_start call the same stages.
  • Fix: one procedure adds a tab to a window: tab_adopt(app, window, tab). It writes tab_ids. tab_new and the tests call it. A test that needs a tab with no page calls tab_new_bare(app, title).
  • Fix: a lint in test_all, beside lint_address.odin: no new(App), new(browser.App), new(Tab), new(Browser_Window) or App{ outside the files of the constructors.
  • The design test: add an invariant to tab_new and run the unit tests. With one constructor, no test fails.

#5.2 Marks that hide a defect

Each mark below says "cause not found" or "to be understood". Each hides a possible product defect.

LocationMarkReason givenJudgment
steps.odin:331flaky on the_caret_blinks_while_the_page_is_busy"failed once on the CI... nothing found"The test samples a 200 ms blink with real waits of 90 ms (busy_page.odin:58-60, :408). The result depends on the frame times. Use the test's clock (1.2), then remove the mark.
steps.odin:301.No_CI on frames_at_rest"the caret drew 5 frames for 3 flips once: cause not found"A possible defect of the product: an extra frame. The test counts frames in real time. Count frames per caret flip on a virtual clock, then run it on the CI.
steps.odin:355.No_CI on setup"the running copy was not out of the way once: cause not found"A possible race in the uninstall of a running copy. Users can meet it. Keep the mark, open an issue, log the file operations in the test.
steps.odin:357.No_CI on crash reports"overflow_thread left no report once: cause not found"A crash report that is lost is a product defect. Run the step on the CI as .Flaky with its log uploaded: a skipped step gives no data.
steps.odin:306.No_CI on dnd"without a GPU... the read-back stays pending. To be understood."A read-back that never completes on a software adapter is a product defect for users with no GPU.
steps_linux.odin:17idb unit tests not run"two of them fail on the GitHub runner and pass in WSL; not understood yet"The two tests are about a failed request and a failed write. Probably a file-system difference. The whole package is skipped for two tests: run the others with ODIN_TEST_NAMES.
ci.yml:55-56three checks removed from the CIfailed under loadCorrect for the two that measure time. Verify that each is behind -Perf and still runs somewhere.
steps.odin:285, :337.No_CI on devtools_resize, real_windowthe runner's screen and scaleLegitimate: a real window depends on the machine.
steps.odin:297, :315.No_CI on video_layers, devtools_split160 s and 420 s of CPU on the software rasterizerLegitimate cost. Both read pixels.
wpt/expectations79 lines with A|Bflaky expectationsAcceptable in number. List them in the report, so that the number does not grow unseen.

Rule to add to docs/testing.md: a .Flaky or .No_CI mark with no known cause has an issue number and still runs somewhere with its logs kept. A mark of type .Flaky is preferable to a skip: it gives data.

#5.3 Assertions on real time in default tests

  • examples/jsdom/animations.html:22: document.timeline.currentTime within 50 ms of performance.now(). It failed on the CI with 144 ms against 220 ms (ci_win2.log, step "DOM for JavaScript"). The two clocks are read at different moments of a frame. Fix: assert the relation that the specification gives (currentTime <= performance.now(), and equal to the frame's time), or run the page on the virtual clock.
  • src/tools/e2e/web_net.odin:365 and :370: a request "left the queue" before or after BURST_SERVER_MS / 2 (200 ms). On a loaded runner an HTTP/2 request can take more than 200 ms to start. Fix: assert the order of events with a gate: the server holds the first answers, and the test counts the requests that have arrived.
  • src/tools/e2e/busy_page.odin:37 and :56: "moved at least 8 px in 300 ms", "clock within 150 ms". Fix: busy_clock.
  • src/tools/e2e/webgl_process.odin:264: an answer within 60 s. This is a bound that only fails a hang. Good.
  • src/webaudio/worklet_test.odin:178 and :226: under 30 s and 15 s. These are bounds, not measures. Good.

#5.4 Global state shared between tests

  • The web tests share one world per process (web_harness.odin:57-71). The last test, zz_the_process_ends_with_nothing_left, depends on the alphabetical order of core:testing (runner.odin:375). A test that leaves a page open makes that last test fail, not itself.
  • Fix: check the leak at the end of each test, in end(): the count of live pages and of tracked bytes returns to its value at begin. The failure then names the test. Keep the last test for the world itself.
  • web_harness.odin:186: virtual_clock uses a @(static) clock. Correct with one thread. It is one more reason why these tests cannot run in parallel in one process.
  • src/browser/main.odin:330 and :355: the tab ids come from a process-wide counter, by design. Unit tests of browser run on several threads, so a test must not assert an id value. chrome_world.odin:116 writes ids 1, 2, 3 by hand, which can collide with ids from tab_new. Fix: tab_new_bare of 5.1 takes the id from the counter.
  • steps.odin:254: the decoder pool of images (see 3.4).

#5.5 Dependence on map order and on addresses

  • Odin seeds the hash of a map from the address of its data. The order of iteration changes with the allocator, the build and the run. The recent layout failure came from this.
  • No test file was found that asserts on the order of a map directly. The risk is in product code whose output is ordered by a map iteration.
  • Fix: a lint for for ... in <map> in src/layout, src/style, src/dom, src/page, with an allow-list for loops whose result does not depend on order (a sum, a lookup, a free). core:odin/parser is already in test_all (lint_test_inits.odin), and gives the type of the iterated expression's declaration in most cases.
  • Fix: the poisoned unit steps already change every address between passes. Keep layout and style there: they are the tests that find this class of defect.

#5.6 Dependence on the machine

  • Fonts: the web tests use fixed fake metrics (web_harness.odin:177-181). Good. The chrome world loads embedded fonts (chrome_world.odin:96-99). Good. The end-to-end sessions use the system's fonts through the browser: text_decoration.odin reads pixels of text. Verify that it sets an embedded font for every text that it measures.
  • GPU: e2e.start(t, {software = true}) exists. Tests that compare pixels to a level must use it on every machine, so that a developer's GPU and the runner's rasterizer give one result.
  • Theme: forced to dark in e2e.odin:213. Good.
  • Locale: no test was found that sets or reads the system's locale. src/i18n has no test file: it is only type-checked on Linux (steps_linux.odin:18).
  • Network: tasks.odin:237 fetches https://example.com/ in the network stress of a full run. Every step inherits WREN_NETWORK_LOOPBACK_ONLY=1. Either the case fails, or fetch.exe ignores the variable. Verify, then remove the case or serve it from the test server.

#5.7 Tests that assert little

  • src/browser/bench_text_test.odin:67: testing.expect(t, best > 0). It is opt-in, so it costs nothing.
  • src/browser/remote_test.odin:153: process_uptime_ms() > 0. It proves only that the call returns.
  • The web tests have a strong rule here: close_page fails a section that ran fewer checks than it declares (web_harness.odin:273). Extend the idea to the end-to-end tests: test_all counts tests, not checks (docs/testing.md). A scenario with no testing.expect* passes. Fix: e2e.end_of_test fails a test that made no check, with a counter that the expect wrappers of e2e increase.

#Order of work

  1. ci.yml: step timeout, upload of logs, Go and engine caches (2.1, 4.3, 4.4). Half a day. No risk.
  2. Scheduler: tasks that can be killed, limits per step, circuit breaker, run budget (2.1, 2.3, 2.4).
  3. Split of the Windows job (3.1).
  4. Deadlines of 60 s and the broken flag in the web harness (2.2), after a measure of the longest barrier.
  5. One constructor for App and its lint (5.1).
  6. Sessions with no pixels (4.1).
  7. WPT and test262 bounds (2.5, 2.6).
  8. The marks of 5.2, one issue each.
  9. The real waits of section 1, with the lint patterns of 1.10 first so that the list is complete.
